overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 8
overview.pill: Calculating and Interpreting Measures of Center and Variability
overview.text: In this lesson, students develop a deep conceptual and procedural understanding of Comparing Distributions in Module 2: Descriptive Statistics.
outcomes: Students compare two or more distributions in terms of center, variability, and shape.
Students interpret a measure of center as a typical value.
Students interpret the IQR as a description of the variability of the data.
Students answer questions that address differences and similarities for two or more distributions.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 8 Exit Ticket: Comparing Distributions
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

Using the histograms of the population distributions of the United States and Kenya in 2010, approximately what percent of the people in the United States were between 15 and 50 years old? Approximately what percent of the people in Kenya were between 15 and 50 years old?

What 5-year interval of ages represented in the 2010 histogram of the United States age distribution has the most people?

Why is the mean age greater than the median age for people in Kenya?
exitTicket.solution:
Using the histograms of the population distributions of the United States and Kenya in 2010, approximately what percent of the people in the United States were between 15 and 50 years old? Approximately what percent of the people in Kenya were between 15 and 50 years old?

Approximately 47% of people in the United States were between 15 and 50 years old. Approximately 48% of people in Kenya were between 15 and 50 years old.

What 5-year interval of ages represented in the 2010 histogram of the United States age distribution has the most people?

The 5-year interval of ages with the most people is the people 45 to 50 years old.

Why is the mean age greater than the median age for people in Kenya?

The mean age is a balance point. The distribution is skewed to the right, and the value of the mean is affected by the older ages in the upper tail of the Kenya population histogram. The mean is greater than the median in this case.

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Master Comparing Distributions through authentic curriculum practice problems. Check your work using the expandable teacher solution key below.

problems.prompt:
The following box plot summarizes ages for a random sample from a made-up country named Math Country.

Make up your own sample of forty ages that could be represented by the box plot for Math Country. Use a dot plot to represent the ages of the forty people in Math Country.
problems.solution: Many possible dot plots would be correct. Analyze individually. Ten of the ages need to be between 0 and 25 years old, ten of the ages need to be between 25 and 40 years old, ten of the ages need to be between 40 and 70 years old, and ten of the ages need to between 70 and 90 years old.

problems.prompt: Is the sample of forty ages represented in your dot plot of Math Country the only sample that could be represented by the box plot? Explain your answer.
problems.solution: There are many possible dot plots that might be represented by this box plot. Any data set with the same 5-number summary would result in this same box plot.

problems.prompt:
The following is a dot plot of sixty ages from a random sample of people from Japan in 2010.

Draw a box plot over this dot plot.
problems.solution: The following is the box plot of the ages of the sample of people from Japan:

problems.prompt: Based on your box plot, would the median age of people in Japan be closer to the median age of people in Kenya or the United States? Justify your answer.
problems.solution: The median age of Japan would be closer to the median age of the United States than to the median age of Kenya. The box plot indicates that the median age of Japan is approximately 45 years old. This median age is even greater than the median age of the United States.

problems.prompt: What does the box plot of this sample from Japan indicate about the possible differences in the age distributions of people from Japan and Kenya?
problems.solution: A much greater percent of the people in Japan are in the older age groups than is the case for Kenya.
